common_meaning: The direction toward the rising sun, opposite west; also the eastern part of a place, or (as "the East") Asia.
example: The sun rises in the east.
rrgm_bridge: East is the direction of sunrise, and also a name others have given to a large and varied part of the world.
invariant_mi: The direction opposite west, or a region lying that way.

domain_entries.PHY: Cardinal direction, where the sun rises.
domain_entries.REL: "The East" was named from a European point of view; it lumps together very different cultures.

count_condition: A direction or region oriented eastward.
transfer_boundary: "The East" is not one culture; the term reflects where the namer stood.

common_meaning: Precisely; without error; also used to agree strongly.
example: The train left at exactly nine; "Exactly!"
rrgm_bridge: Exactly closes the gap between a description and what it describes.
invariant_mi: With no deviation from the stated value or description.

domain_entries.LIN: As a reply, signals full agreement.

count_condition: A description, measure or claim meant to match precisely.
transfer_boundary: Saying "exactly" does not make a figure exact; precision has to be shown. Agreement with "exactly" may be enthusiasm rather than checked agreement.

common_meaning: Relating to the economy, or to the production and use of money and resources; also profitable.
rrgm_bridge: Economic names the domain of how resources are made, moved and shared.
invariant_mi: Concerning the production, distribution and use of resources.

domain_entries.REL: Economic decisions distribute gains and losses among people.

count_condition: A matter of economy or resources.
transfer_boundary: "Economic" (about the economy) differs from "economical" (thrifty). An economic gain overall can be a loss for many people.

common_meaning: The formal process of choosing a person or group for a position, especially by voting.
rrgm_bridge: An election converts many individual choices into one recorded decision about who holds power.
invariant_mi: A formal choice of office-holders by vote.

domain_entries.REL: Elections grant authority and allow peaceful transfer of power.
domain_entries.FOR: Electoral systems differ: first-past-the-post, proportional, ranked choice; each turns the same votes into different results.

count_condition: A procedure in which eligible voters choose among candidates or options.
transfer_boundary: Winning an election grants authority, not correctness. Who is allowed to vote decides whose choice counts.

common_meaning: An event or period in a series; one part of a series on television or radio.
example: I watched the first episode; a brief episode of illness.
rrgm_bridge: An episode is one bounded part of a longer sequence.
invariant_mi: A distinct part of a series or sequence.

domain_entries.LIN: Unit of a broadcast or podcast series.
domain_entries.BIO: An episode of an illness is a bounded period of symptoms.

count_condition: One part within a sequence of events or a series.
transfer_boundary: One episode does not define the whole series, or the whole person.

common_meaning: Without difficulty; also by far; also very possibly.
example: She easily passed; it's easily the best café in town.
rrgm_bridge: Easily marks low resistance, or a wide margin.
invariant_mi: With little effort, or by a large margin.
count_condition: An action done with little effort, or a clear margin.
transfer_boundary: What is easy for one person is not easy for another.

common_meaning: The tools, machines or other things needed for a particular activity.
rrgm_bridge: Equipment is what a task needs in hand.
invariant_mi: The set of tools and devices for an activity.
transfer_boundary: Good equipment does not replace skill.

common_meaning: In the end, after a long time or a series of events.
rrgm_bridge: Eventually places an outcome at the end of a delay.
invariant_mi: At some later time, after delay.
transfer_boundary: "Eventually" gives no date; a promise of eventually can mean never.

common_meaning: The system of production, trade and money in a country or region; also careful use of resources.
example: The economy grew last year; economy class.
rrgm_bridge: An economy is the whole web of making, trading and spending in a place.
invariant_mi: A system of production and exchange, or thrift.

domain_entries.ECO: Measured by output, jobs, prices and trade.
domain_entries.REL: Economic policy distributes gains and losses.

count_condition: A system of production and exchange, or careful use.
transfer_boundary: A growing economy can leave many people worse off; averages hide distribution.

common_meaning: A senior manager in a business; also the branch of government that carries out laws; as an adjective, having power to act.
example: The executive team; the executive branch.
rrgm_bridge: The executive is the part of a structure that acts, as against the parts that decide rules or judge.
invariant_mi: One with authority to carry out decisions, or the branch that enforces law.

domain_entries.REL: Separation of powers divides executive, legislative and judicial roles.

count_condition: A senior manager, or the governing branch that executes law.
transfer_boundary: Executive power checked by courts and legislatures is the basic design; unchecked, it concentrates.
